key_findings: S. aureus alpha-hemolysin activates TRPV1+ nociceptors to release CGRP, which acts via RAMP1 on synovial macrophages to suppress antimicrobial responses.
RAMP1 knockout, TRPV1+ nociceptor ablation, or CGRP receptor antagonist BIBN4096 reduced bacterial load and joint damage.
